jordan.m: Hi all — accepted the GitHub org invite from my phone but the link in my mobile mail client truncated the query string. Now the invite page says 'Invalid invitation'. Can someone reissue or suggest a workaround?
alexa-peopleops: welcome Jordan! Sorry about that. We see mobile clients sometimes wrap long links. @it-support-bot can you resend and also drop the invitation id here so Jordan can accept with the GH CLI if needed?
it-support-bot: Resending now (2026-11-02T16:02:10Z). New invite sent to jordan.m@redwood.ai. Invitation ID: 84217. If the mobile link truncates again, you can accept via the GitHub CLI: `gh api /user/repository_invitations --method PATCH -f invitation_id=84217` while authenticated to the email you intend to use.
jordan.m: thanks. Quick Q: I tried the CLI command but get 'Must be authenticated'. I logged into `gh` with my personal account earlier. How do I switch to the new work account temporarily?
it-support-bot: Two options: 1) `gh auth login --hostname github.com --web` and pick the work account when the browser opens, or 2) run `gh auth logout` then `gh auth login --web` to re-authenticate. If you prefer not to logout, use an incognito window and `gh auth login --web` which will create a separate session for the work account.
sam-eng: Another trick: if you have the invite id, you can accept it from the web by visiting `https://github.com/orgs/redwood/invitation?invitation_id=84217` while signed into the correct account. That avoids relying on the email link.
devex-nia: FYI, if the CLI still complains, check `gh auth status` to confirm which account token is active. If your personal token is cached in VSCode, restart the editor after switching.
jordan.m: used `gh auth login --web` in incognito and accepted via CLI command. I can see myself as a 'member' in the org but can't access private repos yet (404).
\italexa? (excluded)
it-support-bot: If you're 'member' but no teams, it's usually SCIM/SSO pending. I see your account is in the org but SSO is pending because Okta hasn't provisioned you — likely because the employee attribute 'start_date' is missing in the IdP mapping and our SCIM rule filters on it. @alexa-peopleops can you confirm the Okta profile has start_date set?
alexa-peopleops: Good catch. I forgot to set start_date for Jordan while provisioning. I've updated Okta with start_date=2026-11-01 and triggered a SCIM sync.
it-support-bot: Manual SCIM sync requested at 2026-11-02T16:10:05Z. After sync, SSO should be approved and team memberships will appear.
jordan.m: Teams showed up. Trying to clone now but `git clone` fails with permission denied (publickey). I uploaded my SSH key to the account — any ideas?
sam-eng: Run `ssh -T git@github.com -vvv` to see which key is offered. If your agent is presenting a different key (personal), either `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work` or add a `~/.ssh/config` entry: `Host github.com\n  HostName github.com\n  User git\n  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work`.
devex-nia: Also double-check you added the key to the correct GitHub account (work one). Sometimes folks add to personal by accident during the setup flow.
jordan.m: fixed the ssh-agent, can clone now and opened an infra/repo-access request to get write on redwood/docs for a tiny PR. How long do approvals take?
alexa-peopleops: infra usually approves small doc requests same-day. If it's blocking you, ping @sam-eng on the request.
jordan.m: Great — thanks everyone. Lesson learned: mobile mail clients can mangle long invite URLs; CLI + explicit invitation id saved the day. :tada:
